items.description: Python arbitrary-precision integers are represented only inside the declared signed-int64 domain.
items.containment: The sealed 14A domain and helpers remain exact. Required-keyword-only binding changes only the admitted formal kind and association between already-proved actuals and formals; it cannot widen a represented integer value.
items.next_decision: Any broader integer representation or checked arithmetic remains a separately approved future evaluation.

items.description: C division and remainder are undefined for zero and INT64_MIN divided by negative one, while Python has defined failure or arbitrary-precision behavior.
items.containment: A floor-arithmetic expression used as a keyword actual retains its sealed 14A fact, literal-divisor proof, helper version, prerequisite placement, and source-order staging.
items.next_decision: Do not alter the sealed divisor proof or helpers during 14D.

items.description: General Python exceptions, arithmetic failures, call-binding TypeError, raise/assert, and unwinding have no approved C runtime representation.
items.containment: 14D admits only statically complete valid required-keyword-only bindings and rejects invalid declarations or calls before C IR. It adds no runtime binder, default evaluation, propagation, cleanup, or failure channel.
items.next_decision: A separately approved exception mini-phase must specify propagation, cleanup, ownership, traceback limits, and cancellation before any implementation.

items.description: Prerequisite temporaries inside Boolean and chained-comparison conditional regions must remain inside their exact Python reachability guards.
items.containment: A required-keyword-only actual may compose with an independently proved sealed 14B region. Its complete prerequisite closure stages at the actual's source position, and no prerequisite may be hoisted across the fact-owned guard.
items.next_decision: Do not alter 14B region selection, guard polarity, rolling-middle reuse, fact schema, or historical generated C during 14D.

items.description: Direct and mutual recursion lack a separately budgeted resource and termination contract.
items.containment: Required-keyword-only binding feeds the same closed call graph and cannot make a recursive edge eligible. PYC2920 retains precedence.
items.next_decision: Retain clean rejection unless a separately approved bounded recursion contract is proposed.

items.description: Formatting, concatenation, allocation, encoding failure, and owned string lifetime are outside the borrowed-literal string boundary.
items.containment: A string actual bound to a required keyword-only formal must already satisfy the borrowed immutable const-char representation and exact formal category. Formal kind adds no string operation or ownership change.
items.next_decision: Evaluate f-strings and advanced string operations independently with representation, allocation, cleanup, and failure budgets.

items.description: Defaults, keyword arguments, keyword-only parameters, variadics, and unpacking require richer deterministic binding and evaluation rules.
items.containment: The sealed 14C binder remains exact. 14D adds only otherwise eligible declarations with one or more exactly annotated required keyword-only formals and direct calls that cover them explicitly by name. Values stage once in source order and pure references enter C in full formal order. Positional and keyword-only defaults, omitted formals, variadics, unpacking, runtime binding, range, record constructors, dynamic targets, and recursion remain rejected.
items.next_decision: Implement and independently validate parameter-kind facts, required coverage, diagnostic precedence, C prototype/definition formal order, source-order actual staging, formal-order reference assembly, linear resources, cancellation, observers, mappings, and exact historical compatibility before promotion.

items.description: Comprehensions and pattern matching introduce hidden scopes, conditional binding, iteration, and failure-sensitive control flow.
items.containment: Required-keyword-only parameters add one statically known formal kind and no source scope, iteration, conditional binding, or pattern behavior. Comprehension and Match forms remain rejected.
items.next_decision: Give each family a separate feasibility classification; acceptance of required keyword-only calls authorizes neither.

items.description: Context managers and finally regions require exact cleanup ordering across normal, failure, return, break, continue, and cancellation paths.
items.containment: 14D stages only predecessor-owned no-new-cleanup actual values. It adds no cleanup stack, context protocol, finally region, default lifetime, or ownership transfer.
items.next_decision: Do not open until an exception and cleanup-region architecture is separately approved.

items.description: Generators and async syntax require suspension state, retained locals, resumption, ownership, cancellation, and scheduler boundaries.
items.containment: Yield, yield-from, await, async functions, async iteration, and async calls remain rejected. A required-keyword-only binding fact creates no retained or resumable state.
items.next_decision: Require a dedicated state-machine architecture and resource model before any feature implementation.

items.description: Closures, nonlocal capture, lambdas, decorators, and indirect callables require environment objects or import-time callable transformation.
items.containment: Only an already-resolved direct top-level source-function binding is eligible. Assignment-created aliases, attributes, callable values, closures, lambdas, decorators, and indirect targets remain rejected regardless of formal kind.
items.next_decision: Evaluate lexical closure representation independently; decorators remain deferred unless their execution timing is separately modeled.

items.description: Destructuring, starred assignment, assignment expressions, global/nonlocal mutation, and deletion can alter binding lifetime and control-visible state.
items.containment: A required keyword-only parameter is an existing function-scope parameter binding, and its call association is static metadata. No local, global, nonlocal, destructuring, deletion, assignment-expression, or starred target is opened.
items.next_decision: Evaluate fixed scalar binding forms separately; defer global, nonlocal, deletion, and starred forms.

items.description: Sets, dynamic operations, comprehensions, slicing, mutation, aliasing, and escape exceed fixed local container ownership.
items.containment: Only an already-proved scalar container read may appear as an actual. Container values cannot become parameters or escape; the required keyword-only formal profile adds no mutation, dynamic lookup, or ownership behavior.
items.next_decision: Any evaluated operation receives its own capacity, representation, ownership, failure, and helper decision.

items.description: General classes require identity, inheritance, dispatch, descriptors, mutation, allocation, aliasing, and lifecycle semantics absent from static records.
items.containment: Static-record constructors do not participate in 14D keyword binding. Only an already-proved scalar field read may be an actual; general objects, methods, and dynamic attributes remain rejected.
items.next_decision: Remain deferred unless a future roadmap explicitly reopens the general object model with a complete runtime architecture.
